senses.gloss:
नग न-ग, अस्, m. (fr. न-ग, not moving,
or said to be fr. rt. 1. दह् through change of द् into
न्, Uṇādi-s. V. 61), a mountain; a symbolical ex-
pression for the number seven (because of the seven
principal mountains; cf. कुल-पर्वत); a tree; a
plant in general; a serpent; the sun; (अस्, आ, अम्),
not moving, immovable; [cf. अ-ग.]
—नग-ज, अस्,
आ, अम्, mountain, mountaineer; (अस्), m. ‘mountain-
born,’ an elephant; (आ), f. a species of plant (=
क्षुद्र-पाषाण-भेदा).
—नग-नदी, f. ‘moun-
tain-river,’ N. of a river.
—नग-नन्दिनी, f. an
epithet of the goddess Durgā (‘daughter of the
mountain,’ Durgā being in one of her characters
the daughter of the personified Himālaya).
—नग-
पति, इस्, m. ‘chief of mountains,’ the Himālaya range
of mountains.
—नग-भिद्, त्, m. ‘rock-splitter’ or
‘tree-splitter,’ a species of plant (= पाषाण-भेद-
न), Plectanthrus Scutellaroides; an axe; a crow; Indra.
—नग-भू, ऊस्, ऊस्, उ, ‘mountain-born,’ mountain,
mountaineer; (ऊस्), m. a species of plant, = क्षुद्र-
पाषाण-भेदा, (more probably fem. like नग-जा.)
—नग-मूर्धन्, आ, m. the crest or brow of a
mountain.
—नग-रन्ध्र-कर, अस्, m. ‘rending
the mountains,’ an epithet of Kārttikeya.
—नग-
वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing mountains, abounding in
trees.
—नग-वाहन, अस्, m. ‘whose vehicle is
a mountain, mountain-borne,’ an epithet of Śiva.
[]
—नग-स्वरूपिणी, f. a kind of metre consisting
of four lines of eight syllables each.
—नगाग्र
(˚ग-अग्˚), अम्, n. the summit or top of a mountain.
—नगाटन (˚ग-अट्˚), अस्, m. ‘moving about on
trees,’ a monkey.
—नगाधिप (˚ग-अध्˚), अस्, m.
‘chief of mountains,’ the Himālaya.
—नगाधिराज
(˚ग-अध्˚), अस्, m. = the preceding.
—नगारि (˚ग-
अरि), इस्, m., N. of a man.
—नगावास (˚ग-आव्˚),
अस्, m. ‘living on trees,’ a peacock.
—नगाश्रय
(˚ग-आश्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, living in or frequenting moun-
tains; (अस्), m. a species of bulbous plant growing
on mountains (= हस्ति-कन्द).
—नगाह्वय (˚ग-
आह्˚), अस्, m., N. of a man.
—नगेन्द्र (˚ग-इन्˚),
अस्, m. ‘chief of mountains,’ the Himālaya, Kailāsa.
—नगेश (˚ग-ईश), अस्, m. ‘chief of mountains,’
N. of a particular mountain.
—नगोच्छ्राय (˚ग-
उच्˚), अस्, m. heighth or elevation of a mountain.
—नगौकस् (˚ग-ओक्˚), आस्, m. ‘inhabiting a moun-
tain or tree;’ a lion; the fabulous animal Śarabha;
a bird in general; a crow; [cf. अगौकस्.]

नाग नाग, अस्, m. (perhaps for original
स्नाग; Angl. Sax. snaca; Eng. snake; or connected
with नग, a mountain, or नग्न, naked; said to be
fr. rt. 1. दह् through change of द् into न्), a snake in
general, especially the spectacle-snake or cobra capella,
Coluber; a Nāga or fabulous serpent-demon so
called, having a human face with the tail of a ser-
pent, (the race of these beings is said to have sprung
from Kadrū, wife of Kaśyapa [or from Su-rasā], in
order to people Pātāla, one of the regions below the
earth, their city is called Bhoga-vatī); an elephant;
a shark (= तन्तु-नाग); a cruel or tyrannical
person; (at the end of a comp.) ‘an elephant of a
man,’ any great or pre-eminent person; N. of several
plants, the small tree with fragrant blossoms, Mesua
Roxburghii [cf. नाग-केशर]; Rottlera Tinctoria
(= पुन्-नाग); a Cyperus (= मुस्तक); Piper
Betel; a poisonous plant (see नाग-स्तोकक); a
cloud; a peg or nail projecting from a wall to hang
anything upon; one of the five airs of the body,
that which is expelled by eructation; N. of the
number seven, (probably to be referred to seven
mythical serpents, but eight principal Nāgas are
mentioned); N. of a Sādhya; of a Buddhist teacher;
of a king of Āryāvarta, contemporary of Samudra-
gupta; N. of a dynasty consisting of nine or seven
princes; N. of several men; N. of a mountain; of
a district; (ई), f. a female Nāga; a female elephant;
(अम्), n. tin; lead; one of the astronomical periods
called Karaṇas, (it is one of those termed ध्रुव,
q. v., or invariable, and corresponds to the last half of
Amāvāsya or new moon); the effects of that period
on anything done or happening during it; (अस्, ई,
अम्), formed or consisting of snakes, serpentine,
snaky; relating to serpents or serpent-demons;
[]
elephantine, belonging to or resembling an elephant;
(आ), f., N. of a woman; [cf. क्षिति-न्˚.]
—नाग-
कन्द, अस्, m. a kind of bulbous plant (= हस्ति-
कन्द).
—नाग-कन्यका, f. a serpent-virgin.
—नाग-कर्ण, अस्, m. a kind of Ricinus (= रक्-
तैरण्ड, हस्ति-कर्ण).
—नाग-किञ्जल्क, अम्, n.
the blossom of Mesua Roxburghii.
—नाग-कुमार,
अस्, m. a prince of the serpent-demons; N. of a class
of deities among the Bhavanādhīśas guarding the
treasures of Kuvera.
—नाग-केश, अस्, m., N. of a
minister of king Nageśa.
—नाग-केशर or नाग-
केसर, अस्, m. a small tree with fragrant blossoms
(commonly Nageśar), Mesua Roxburghii or Ferrea;
(अम्), n. the blossom of this tree.
—नाग-खण्ड,
N. of one of the nine divisions of Bhārata-varṣa.
—नाग-गन्धा, f. a species of bulbous plant (=
नाकुली or सर्प-गन्धा).
—नाग-गर्भ, अम्,
n. red lead.
—नाग-चूड, अस्, m. ‘snake-crested’ or
‘whose top-knot consists of snakes,’ an epithet of
Śiva.
—नाग-च्छत्त्रा, f. a kind of plant, Tiaridium
Indicum.
—नाग-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, produced by or born
from a Nāga, &c.; (अम्), n. red lead; tin.
—नाग-
जिह्वा, f. ‘snake-tongue,’ a species of plant, Asclepias
Pseudosarsa; (see शारिवा.)
—नाग-जिह्विका, f. red
arsenic.
—नाग-जीवन, अम्, n. tin.
—नागजीवन-
शत्रु, उस्, m. ‘enemy of tin,’ orpiment.
—नाग-
तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
—नाग-दत्त, अस्,
आ, अम्, given by Nāgas or serpents; (अस्), m., N. of
one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; N. of a man
related to Śākya-muni; of a king of Āryāvarta,
contemporary of Samudra-gupta.
—नाग-दन्त, अस्,
m. elephant's tusk or ivory, the tooth or tusk of an
elephant; a shelf, peg, or bracket projecting from
a wall and used to hang things upon; (आ), f., N. of
an Apsaras; (ई), f. a species of sun-flower, Helio-
tropium Indicum; a harlot.
—नागदन्तक, अस्,
m. ivory; a wooden peg or bracket projecting from
a wall, a shelf; (इका), f. a plant, commonly called
Rāma-dūti, Tragia Involucrata.
—नाग-दमनी, f.
a particular plant (= जम्बू, जाम्बवती, वृक्का).
—नाग-दलोपम (˚ल-उप्˚), अम्, n. the tree
Xylocarpus Granatum.
—नाग-दाशक, अस्, m., N.
of a prince.
—नाग-देण्टिका, f. the betel plant.
—नाग-देव, अस्, m., N. of an author.
—नाग-
द्रु, उस्, m. a species of Euphorbia used in offerings
to the snake-goddess Manasā (= समन्त-दुग्ध).
—नाग-द्वीप, अस्, m., N. of a Dvīpa in Jambū-
khaṇḍa or Bhārata-varṣa.
—नाग-नक्षत्र, अम्,
n., N. of the three asterisms forming the Nāga-
vīthi (?).
—नाग-नाथ, अस्, m. the king of the ser-
pents, a serpent-chief; (अम्), n., N. of a Liṅga sacred
to Śiva; (also called नागनाथेश-लिङ्ग.)
—नाग-
नाभ, अस्, m., N. of a man.
—नाग-नामक, अम्,
n. tin.
—नाग-नामन्, आ, m. holy basil (= तुलसी).
—नाग-नायक, अस्, m. the leader or chief of the
Nāgas or snakes.
—नाग-नासा, f. the trunk or pro-
boscis of an elephant.
—नागनासोरू (˚सा-ऊरू), ऊस्,
f. a woman whose thighs taper like the trunk of an
elephant; [cf. करभोरू, p. 205, col. 2.]
—नाग-
निर्यूह, अस्, m. = निर्यूह and नाग-दन्त, a
large pin or bracket projecting from a wall like a
shelf.
—नाग-पञ्चमी, f. a particular festival, the
fifth day in the light half of month Śrāvaṇa;
the fifth day in the dark half of month Āṣāḍhā.
—नाग-पति, इस्, m. a serpent-chief.
—नाग-पत्-
त्रा, f. = नाग-दमनी.
—नाग-पत्त्री, f. a species
of plant (= लक्ष्मणा).
—नाग-पद, अस्, m. a
kind of coitus.
—नाग-पर्णी, f. the betel plant.
—नाग-पाल, अस्, m., N. of a man; a prince of
Sāśikya.
—नाग-पाश, अस्, m. a sort of magical noose
or lasso used in battle to entangle an enemy; ‘the
serpent-noose,’ an epithet of the weapon of Varuṇa,
regent of the waters; a kind of coitus.
—नाग-
पाशक, अस्, m. a kind of coitus.
—नाग-पुर,
अस्, m. ‘elephant's town,’ ancient Delhi (= गज-
पुर, हास्तिन-पुर).
—नाग-पुष्प, अस्, m.
several plants, = Rottlera Tinctoria (= पुन्-नाग);
Mesua Roxburghii (= नाग-केसर); Michelia
Champaka (= चम्पक); (अम्), n. the blossom of
this plant; (ई), f. = नाग-दमनी.
—नागपुष्प-
फला, f. the plant Benincasa Cerifera (= कुष्-
[]
माण्डी).
—नाग-पुष्पिका, f. yellow jasmine (=
स्वर्ण-यूथी).
—नाग-फल, अस्, m. the plant
Trichosanthes Diœca; (आ), f. a various reading for
नाग-बला.
—नाग-बधू, ऊस्, f. a female ele-
phant.
—नाग-बन्धक, अस्, m. an elephant-
catcher.
—नाग-बन्धु, उस्, m. ‘elephant-friend,
liked by elephants,’ the holy fig-tree, Ficus Religiosa
(= अश्वत्थ).
—नाग-बल, अस्, m. ‘having the
strength of an elephant,’ an epithet of Bhīma; (आ),
f. the plant Uraria Lagopodioides; (अम्), n. a par-
ticular high number.
—नाग-बुद्ध, अस्, m. or
नाग-बोधि, इस्, m., N. of a Buddhist teacher.
—नाग-बुद्धि, इस्, m., N. of a medical author.
—नाग-बोध, अस्, m., N. of an author.
—नाग-
भगिनी, f. ‘serpent's sister,’ N. of the goddess Manasā;
[cf. नाग-मातृ.]
—नाग-भिद्, त्, m. ‘elephant-
destroyer,’ a species of snake, Amphisbæna; (also
written नाग-भृत्, = डुण्डु.)
—नाग-भूषण,
अस्, आ, अम्, ‘decorated with serpents,’ an epithet of
Śiva; [cf. नाग-चूड.]
—नाग-भोग, अस्, m. a
species of serpent.
—नाग-मण्डलिक, अस्, m. a
snake-keeper; a snake-catcher.
—नाग-मती, f. the
plant Ocimum Sanctum.
—नाग-मय, अस्, ई, अम्,
consisting of or in elephants.
—नाग-मल्ल, अस्,
m. ‘an athlete among the elephants,’ an epithet of
Indra's elephant Airāvata.
—नाग-मातृ, ता, f.
‘mother of serpent-demons,’ an epithet of Su-rasā; an
epithet of the goddess Manasā (supposed to preside
over snakes); red arsenic.
—नाग-मार, अस्, m. a
species of pot-herb, also Keśa-rāja.
—नाग-मुद्र,
अस्, m., N. of a Buddhist Sthavira (= नाग-सेन).
—नाग-यष्टि, इस्, f. or नाग-यष्टिका, f. a gradu-
ated pole or post for showing the depth of water in
a newly dug pond, a boring-rod or stick driven into
the earth.
—नाग-रक्त, अम्, n. red lead.
—नाग-
रङ्ग, अस्, m. the orange, (usually applied to the
Silhet orange, Citrus Aurantium.)
—नाग-रट्ट, अस्,
m. a various reading for नाग-वट्ट, q. v.
—नाग-
राज्, ट्, m. a serpent-king, a chief of the Nāgas.
—नाग-राज, अस्, m. ‘king of the serpents,’ an epithet
of Ananta or of Vāsuki, chief of the serpents; a king
among the elephants, a large elephant.
—नागराज-
कर, अस्, m. the trunk of the king of elephants.
—नाग-राजन्, आ, m. a serpent-king.
—नाग-रुक,
अस्, m. = नाग-रङ्ग, the orange-tree.
—नाग-रेणु,
उस्, m. red lead.
—नाग-लता, f. the penis; N. of a
woman.
—नाग-लेखा, f., N. of a woman.
—नाग-
लोक, अस्, m. the Nāga world or one of the regions
below the earth, otherwise called Pātāla, the world of
the serpent-demons, the abode of serpents or the
race of serpents collectively.
—नाग-वट्ट, अस्, m.,
N. of a man; [cf. नाग-रट्ट.]
—नाग-वत्, आन्, अती,
अत्, consisting of snakes; possessed of elephants.
—ना-
ग-वधू, see नाग-बधू.
—नाग-वन, अम्, n.
‘serpent-wood,’ N. of a place.
—नाग-वर्त्मन्, आ,
m., N. of a Tīrtha.
—नाग-वल्लरी or नाग-
वल्लि, इस्, ई, or नाग-वल्लिका, f. Piper Betel, the
betel plant.
—नाग-वारिक, अस्, m. a royal elephant;
an elephant-driver or keeper; a peacock; an epithet
of Garuḍa, the bird of Viṣṇu; the chief person in a
court or assembly.
—नाग-वास, अस्, m. ‘abode of
snakes,’ N. of a lake supposed to have been formed
originally by the valley of Nepal.
—नाग-वीथी, f. a
row of serpents; the serpents' path, that part of the
moon's path which contains the asterisms Svāti or
(according to others) Aśvinī, Bharaṇī, and Kṛttikā;
N. of a daughter of Yāmī who was the daughter of
Dakṣa and wife of Dharma; of a daughter of Kaś-
yapa by Yāminī.
—नाग-वृक्ष, अस्, m. a species
of tree.
—नाग-शत, अस्, m., N. of a mountain.
—नाग-श्री, ईस्, f., N. of a queen.
—नाग-सम्-
भव, अम्, n. minium or red lead.
—नाग-सम्-
भूत, ‘produced from serpents,’ epithet of a sort of
pearl.
—नाग-साह्वय, अस्, आ, अम्, called after
elephants, (generally with नगर = ‘elephant's town,’
i. e. Hāstina-pura.)
—नाग-सुगन्धा, f. the ich-
neumon plant (= सु-गन्धा, सर्प-सुगन्धा,
भुजङ्गाक्षी; cf. नाकुली).
—नाग-सेन, अस्, m.,
N. of a Buddhist Sthavira; a king of Āryāvarta and
contemporary of Samudra-gupta.
—नाग-स्तोकक,
अम्, n. a species of poisonous plant.
—नाग-स्थल,
[]
N. of a village near Mathurā.
—नाग-स्फोता or
rather नाग-स्फोटा, f. two plants (= दन्ती and नाग-
दन्ती).
—नाग-स्वरूपिणी, f. a kind of metre con-
sisting of four lines of eight syllables each.
—नाग-
हनु, उस्, m. a kind of perfume (= नख).
—नाग-
हन्त्री, f. a species of plant (= बन्ध्या-कर्को-
टकी; cf. नागाराति).
—नाग-ह्रद, अम्, n. a
lake inhabited by snakes or serpent-demons.
—ना-
गाख्य (˚ग-आख्˚), अस्, m. = नाग-केसर, Mesua
Roxburghii.
—नागाङ्ग, अम्, n. Hāstina-pura.
—ना-
गाङ्गना (˚ग-अङ्˚), f. a female elephant; the pro-
boscis of an elephant; [cf. नागाञ्जना.]
—नागाञ्-
चला (˚ग-अञ्˚), f. = नाग-यष्टि, q. v.
—नागाञ्-
जना, f. the female of an elephant (= नाग-यष्टि,
q. v.).
—नागाधिप (˚ग-अध्˚), अस्, m. ‘the ser-
pent-prince,’ an epithet of Śeṣa.
—नागाधिपति
(˚ग-अध्˚), इस्, m. ‘serpent-chief,’ an epithet of
Virūḍhaka.
—नागाधिराज (˚ग-अध्˚), अस्, m. the
king or chief of the elephants.
—नागानन्द
(˚ग-आन्˚), अस् or अम्, m. n. (?), or नागानन्द-ना-
टक, अम्, n., N. of a play ascribed to king Harṣa.
—नागान्तक (˚ग-अन्˚), अस्, m. ‘destroyer of
serpents,’ an epithet of Garuḍa, the bird of Viṣṇu.
—नागाभिभु, उस्, or -भू (˚ग-अभ्˚), ऊस्, m., N.
of a Buddha.
—नागाराति (˚ग-अर्˚), इस्, m. a species
of plant (= बन्ध्या-कर्कोटकी; cf. नाग-हन्त्री).
—नागारि (˚ग-अरि), इस्, m. ‘enemy of serpents,’
epithet of Garuḍa.
—नागारूढ (˚ग-आर्˚), अस्, आ,
अम्, mounted or riding upon an elephant.
—नागार्-
जुन (˚ग-अर्˚), अस्, m., N. of an ancient Buddhist
teacher of the rank of a Bodhi-sattva, said to be
the author of the Yoga-ratna-mālā or Āścarya-ratna-
mālā; (ई), f., N. of a rock-cavern.
—नागालाबु
(˚ग-अल्˚), उस्, f. a species of gourd (= कुम्भ-
तुम्बि).
—नागाशन (˚ग-अश्˚), अस्, m. ‘snake-
eater,’ a peacock; an epithet of Garuḍa.
—ना-
गाह्व (˚ग-आह्˚), अम्, n. ‘the town called after
elephants,’ Hāstina-pura; (आ), f. a species of bulbous
plant (= लक्ष्मणा; cf. नाग-पत्त्री).
—नागाह्-
वय (˚ग-आह्˚), अस्, m. a species of plant; an epithet
of Tathāgata-bhadra.
—नागेन्द्र (˚ग-इन्˚), अस्,
m. a serpent-prince, serpent-chief; (ई), f., N. of a
river.
—नागेश (˚ग-ईश), अस्, m., N. of a prince;
an epithet of Patañjali; नागेश or नागेश-भट्ट,
N. of a grammarian, see नागोजी; (अम्), n., N. of a
Liṅga in Dārukā-vana.
—नागेश्वर (˚ग-ईश्˚), अस्,
m., N. of a man; (ई), f., N. of the deity Manasā;
(अम्), n., N. of a Liṅga.
—नागेश्वर-तीर्थ, अम्,
n., N. of several sacred bathing-places.
—नागोदर
(˚ग-उद्˚), अस्, m., N. of a medical author; (अम्),
n. a medical term for a peculiar disease of preg-
nancy, dissolution of the fetus in the womb; a
breast-plate, a cuirass.
—नागोद्भेद (˚ग-उद्˚), अस्,
m., N. of a sacred spot where the river Saras-vatī
re-appears.

नगणा नगणा, f. a plant, Cardiospermum
Halicacabum; (also read नग्ना.)

नगर नगर, अम्, ई (fr. न-ग?), n. f. a
town, city, (often appended to the names of cities in
India or standing alone as a name.) According to
Pāṇ. VIII. 4, 39, the initial न् cannot be cerebralized
[cf. गिरि-नगर]; at the end of adj. comps. the
fem. may end in आ (e. g. स-ग्राम-नगरा मेदिनी,
the earth with its villages and cities).
—नगर-
काक, अस्, m. ‘a crow in a town,’ an expression of
contempt; [cf. नगर-वायस.]
—नगर-कोटि,
N. of a place; N. of a town at the foot of the Himā-
laya, Nagar-kot.
—नगर-घात, अस्, आ, अम्, town-
destroying; (अस्), m. an elephant.
—नगर-घा-
तक, अस्, m. the destroyer of a city.
—नगर-जन,
अस्, m. towns-folk; a citizen.
—नगर-द्वार, अम्,
n. the gate of a town, city-gate.
—नगर-धन-वि-
हार, अस्, m., N. of a Buddhist monastery.
—नगर-
पति, इस्, m. the chief of a town.
—नगर-पुर,
अम्, n., N. of a town.
—नगर-प्रदक्षिणा, f.
carrying an idol round a city in procession; [cf. प्र-
दक्षिणा.]
—नगर-प्रान्त, अस्, m. the outskirts
of a town.
—नगर-मर्दिन्, ई, m. ‘town-crusher,’
N. of a man.
—नगर-मालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, garlanded
with cities.
—नगर-मुस्ता, f. = नगरोत्था; [cf.
नागर-मुस्ता.]
—नगर-रक्षा, f. superintend-
ence or government of a town.
—नगररक्षा-
धिकृत (˚क्षा-अध्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, appointed to
the government of a town.
—नगर-रक्षिन्,
ई, m. the governor or superintendent of a town,
civic-guard, town-watchman.
—नगर-वायस, अस्,
m. = नगर-काक.
—नगर-वासिन्, ई, इनी, इ, in-
habiting towns, dwelling in cities, citizen.
—नगर-
वाह्य, अस्, आ, अम्, situated without the town.
—नग-
र-सम्मित, अस्, आ, अम्, equal to a town.
—नगर-
स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, city-dwelling; a resident in a city,
a townsman, citizen, burgess.
—नगर-स्वरूपिणी,
f. a species of the Anu-ṣṭubh metre.
—नगर-
हार, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), ‘town-taking,’ N. of
a kingdom.
—नगराधिकृत (˚र-अध्˚), अस्, m.
the superintendent or governor of a town.
—नगरा-
धिप (˚र-अध्˚), अस्, m. or नगराधिपति, इस्,
m. the chief magistrate of a town, head police-officer.
—नगराध्यक्ष (˚र-अध्˚), अस्, m. the over-
seer or superintendent of a town.
—नगराभ्याश
(˚र-अभ्˚), अस्, m. the neighbourhood of a city.
—नगरी-निरोध, अस्, m., N. of the sixty-third
chapter of the Krīḍā-khaṇḍa or second part of the
Gaṇeśa-Purāṇa.
—नगरी-युक्ति, इस्, f., N. of a
chapter of the Yukti-kalpa-taru ascribed to king
Bhoja.
—नगरी-रक्षिन्, ई, m. = नगर-रक्षिन्.
—नगरी-वक, अस्, m. ‘town-crane,’ a crow.
—नगरोत्था (˚र-उत्था), f. a species of plant, =
नगर-मुस्ता; [cf. नागरोत्था.]
—नगरोपान्त
(˚र-उप्˚), अम्, n. suburb, skirts of a town.
—नग-
रौकस् (˚र-ओक्˚), आस्, m. the inhabitant of a town,
townsman.
—नगरौषधि (˚र-ओष्˚), इस्, f. the
plantain, Musa Sapientum (= कदली).

नागर नागर, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. नगर), town-
born, town-bred, city, citizen; relating or belonging to
a town, civic; spoken in a town or city; polite, civil;
clever, sharp, knowing; bad, vile; nameless; (अस्), m. a
citizen; = पौर, a term for a prince engaged in war
under certain circumstances and (in astrology) applied
to a planet in a state of opposition to other planets; a
husband's brother; an orange; a lecturer; denial of
knowledge; hardship, toil, fatigue; desire of final
beatitude; (ई), f. the Nāgarī or Deva-nāgarī (q. v.)
character in which Sanskrit is commonly written; a
species of Euphorbia (= स्नुही); a clever or crafty
or intriguing woman; (अम्), n. dry ginger; the root
of Cyperus Pertenuis; a sort of coitus.
—नागर-
खण्ड, अस्, m., N. of a section of the Skanda-
Purāṇa.
—नागर-घन, अस्, m. or नागर-मुस्ता,
[]
f. a species of grass, Cyperus.
—नागराह्व (˚र-
आह्˚), अम्, n. dry ginger.
—नागरोत्था (˚र-उत्˚),
f. = नागर-मुस्ता, q. v.

नगराय, Nom. P. नगरायते, &c., to have
the appearance of a town, look like a town.
नगरिन्, ई, m., N. of a man.

नगरीय, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to a town, civic,
city, urban.
नग्न नग्न. See under rt. नज् below.

नग्न, अस्, आ, अम्, naked, nude, bare; uncultivated,
uninhabited, desolate; (अस्), m. a naked mendicant;
a N. of Śiva; a hypocrite (whose nakedness is a
mere pretence); a Buddhist mendicant, = क्षप-
णक; a bard accompanying an army; (2. नग्ना),
f. a naked, wanton woman; a girl before menstru-
ation (and therefore allowed to go naked; cf. नग्-
निका); the plant Cardiospermum Halicacabum; [cf.
नगणा, 1. नग्ना above; Lith. nōga-s, ‘naked;’
Russ. nagiĭ; Slav. nago-ta, ‘nakedness;’ Goth.
naqvaths; Old Iceland. nakt-r; Angl. Sax. nacud,
nacod, genacyan; Old Germ. nachat; Mod. Germ.
nackt; Hib. nochd; Lat. nudus.]
—नग्नङ्-
करण, अस्, ई, अम्, making naked.
—नग्न-जित्, त्,
m., N. of a prince of the Gandhāras, father of one
of Kṛṣṇa's wives; N. of an author of a work on
architecture; of a poet.
—नग्न-ता, f. or नग्न-
त्व, अम्, n. nakedness, nudity.
—नग्नम्-भ-
विष्णु, उस्, उस्, उ, or नग्नम्-भावुक, अस्, आ,
अम्, becoming naked, uncovering one's self in a
shameless manner.
—नग्न-वृत्ति, इस्, f. ‘the men-
dicant's commentary,’ N. of a commentary on the
Uṇādi-sūtras.
—नग्न-व्रत-धर, अस्, m. ‘observ-
ing the vow of a naked mendicant,’ epithet of Śiva.
—नग्नाट or नग्नाटक (˚न-अट्˚), अस्, m. a man
who wanders about naked, especially a Buddhist or
Jaina religious mendicant.
—नग्नी-करण, अम्, n.
making naked, undressing, stripping.
—नग्नी-कृ,
cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्तुम्, to render
naked, to convert into a naked mendicant.
—नग्नी-
कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, made naked, undressed, stripped;
converted into a naked mendicant.

नग्ना 1. नग्ना, f. (for 2. नग्ना see नग्न
below), Ved. speech; (a various reading for नना, q. v.)

नग्नहु नग्नहु, उस्, m. or नग्नहू, ऊस्, m.
ferment, a drug used for fermenting spirituous liquor.

नग्नक, अस्, इका, अम्, naked, wanton; (अस्),
m. a naked mendicant, especially a Buddhist or Jaina
ascetic; a bard; (इका), f. a naked or wanton woman;
a girl before menstruation.

नग्निका, f. a naked woman; a girl before men-
struation or about ten years old.
नागक, अस्, m., N. of a man.

नागिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having serpents, covered with
or surrounded by serpents; snaky.

नागोद, अम्, n. armour for the front of the body;
[cf. नागोदर above.]

नागपैय नागपैय, अस्, m., N. of a poet
mentioned in the Śārṅgadhara-paddhati.
नागम्मा नागम्मा, f., N. of a female poet.

नागरक, अस्, ई, अम्, living in a town, (op-
posed to आरण्यक); clever, cunning; (अस्), m. a
citizen; the chief of the police or of a town; an
artist; a thief, (a various reading for नागरिक);
(अम्), n. dry ginger; [cf. नागर.]

नागरिक, अस्, ई, अम्, town-born, town-bred;
living in or inhabiting a town; produced from a
town; polite; clever, cunning; (अस्), m. a citizen,
the chief of a town, superintendant of police; (अम्),
n. the toll raised from a town.
—नागरिक-पुर,
अम्, n., N. of a town.
—नागरिक-बल, अम्, n.
the guard of a police-officer.
नागरेयक, अस्, ई, अम्, city, citizen.
नागर्य, अम्, n. town-life, shrewdness.

नागरमर्दि नागरमर्दि, इस्, m. (fr. नगर-
मर्दिन्), a patronymic from Nagara-mardin.

नागरीट नागरीट, अस्, m. a libertine, rake,
blackguard; (probably for नागवीट below.)
नागवीट, अस्, m. a rake; intriguer, match-maker.

नागशुण्डी नागशुण्डी, f. a species of gourd;
(also read नामशुण्डी.)
नागुली नागुली, f., N. of a town.

नागोजी नागोजी or नागोजि or नागोजि-भट्ट,
अस्, m., N. of a modern grammarian, also called
नागेश-भट्ट, author of a Vivaraṇa or interpreta-
tion of Kaiyaṭa's commentary on Patañjali, of a
grammar called Paribhāṣendu-śekhara, &c.

नाग्नजित नाग्नजित, अस्, m. (fr. नग्न-जित्),
a descendant of Nagna-jit; (ई), f., N. of one of the
wives of Kṛṣṇa; (wrongly spelt नग्नजिती.)
